newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVERNMENT APPROVES NEW PROFIT TAX RULES.
newsitem.headline: GOVERNMENT APPROVES NEW PROFIT TAX RULES.

text.p: The government has approved new profit tax rules to exempt companies from profit tax for three years until they have covered their losses, Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said on Thursday.
"The amendment will allow the company to transfer its losses to the next fiscal year for up to three years," Vagnorius told a news conference.
The government also approved the levy of a profit tax on payments to foreign companies registered in countries and regions where there is no tax or low tax rates.
"All companies operating in Lithuania will have to pay taxes even those who could avoid it by transferring the profit to low tax zones," Vagnorius said.
The tax will be the difference between the 29 percent profit tax in Lithuania and the profit tax in the low-tax state.
The government also approved cutting the profit tax to 10 percent from 15 percent for foreign companies if they give Lithuanian firms the right to use their trademarks and licences.
